kv.memory.clarity-over-performance: mimid (Mark, 2026-10-17): choose clarity and correctness over raw performance. Prefer the straightforward, readable implementation (clone, allocate, linear scan, simple ownership) unless a measured problem says otherwise; no premature optimization, zero-copy tricks, or unsafe for speed. Mark any known performance ceiling with a ponytail: comment naming the upgrade path.
kv.memory.crypto-backend-policy: mimid: Mark dislikes aws-lc/ring but decided (2026-10-17) NOT to enforce a ban; accept whatever deps pull in (e.g. rustls default provider) and fix later. Do not add cargo-deny bans for ring/aws-lc unless asked.
kv.memory.decompose-just-in-time: mimid: decompose an issue into sub-issues only when it is next on the critical path or becomes ready, not upfront; exception: issues whose content is fixed by a spec (not by our own APIs) may be planned early. Plans are approved by Mark before sub-issues are filed.

kv.memory.hub-landing: mimid (Mark, 2026-10-18): for the hub epic .6 AND the follower epic .7, land each sub-bead as soon as it passes all six gates and any decisions/test changes it raises are approved by Mark; no per-bead landing question. Pushing still needs explicit OK.
kv.memory.lang-and-spec-target: mimid: MIMI reference implementation over MLS (RFC 9420). Language: Rust (decided 2026-10-17). Spec target: implement the LATEST version of each MIMI draft exactly as written, regardless of draft expiry/maturity; where a draft is ambiguous, pick the sane reading and document it.
kv.memory.no-ct-compare-zeroize: mimid (Mark, 2026-10-18): no constant-time comparisons and no hand-added zeroization; use only what libraries already build in. Why: hashed-token lookups by index leak nothing useful (the attacker picks the token, not its hash), and ct_eq after a WHERE hash = ? match is a no-op (.11.1). How to apply: don't add subtle/zeroize or Drop-wipe code; keep redacted Debug (AGENTS.md secret-logging rule still applies).
kv.memory.parallel-target-dir: mimid: every cargo build in a worktree, including LANDING, must use a private CARGO_TARGET_DIR under /home/mark/Cache/ (e.g. /home/mark/Cache/mimid-target-<bead>, /home/mark/Cache/mimid-land-<worktree>), NOT under /tmp (something on the machine deletes files under /tmp mid-build, seen 2026-10-18), and never the shared default /home/mark/Cache/cargo-target (Cargo names workspace-member artifacts by workspace-relative path, so worktrees collide and get stale artifacts). Delete each private target dir after the bead lands (disk is limited).
kv.memory.product-scope: mimid goals (Mark, 2026-10-17; updated 2026-10-18): BOTH (a) MIMI interop/reference target AND (b) usable chat system. Layering rule: MIMI crates (content, room-policy, protocol, mls) are spec-only; product additions (accounts, push, history, C2S API) live in provider/client layers. Clients: no mimid TUI; mimid-agent is the JMAP Chat <-> MIMI bridge for stock JMAP Chat clients (mimid-1wgh.38); the agent is a library (mimid-agent-core) with a desktop daemon wrapper and a future native mobile binding (mimid-1wgh.39, epic mimid-1wgh.40). v1 auth: dev bearer tokens via admin CLI. C2S API: JMAP Chat E2EE subset + mimid MLS key-material capability (mimid-1wgh.9); senderMsgId per R1 (mimid-1wgh.10, kept over the draft). Attachments in v1. Spaces and room directory out of v1.

kv.memory.spec-ambiguity-rule: mimid: every spec ambiguity/contradiction -> bd decision (type decision, child of epic) citing draft+section, competing readings, chosen reading, rationale; code carries a short comment with the decision ID. Never resolve silently.

kv.memory.toolchain-policy: mimid: no MSRV. Support latest stable Rust only and latest crate releases (Mark, 2026-10-17: 'completely fine to need new rust and new crates'). No rust-version field, no MSRV CI job.
kv.memory.verify-before-asking: mimid (Mark, 2026-10-18): before putting any decision or plan to Mark, the orchestrator verifies each recommendation's factual premise itself (grep the code, quote the spec with line numbers) and cites that evidence in the question. Never relay a subagent's rationale unchecked, and never batch decisions into one 'accept all' unless every premise is verified. Plans get an independent spec/code review before approval. Why: on 2026-10-18 Mark had to intervene via another session on JM-8 (the hub CAN read room_name), the ChatContact.id scope (understated as a two-line change), F-Q5 (protocol-06 §5.5 unread) and JM-4 (text/plain nonconformance, .9 WSS drift).
kv.memory.wg-feedback: mimid (Mark, 2026-10-17): accumulate errata and suggestions for the specs (MIMI drafts, mls-extensions, ratchet-tree-options, RFC 9420, mlswg test vectors) as beads the moment they are found: type task, label wg plus spec:<doc-rev> (e.g. spec:mimi-protocol-06), title 'wg: <doc> <section> <issue>', description = draft+section, what the text says, the problem, what mimid did (decision ID), suggested fix. Every decision bead that exposes a spec defect or ambiguity gets a companion wg bead. Agents report such items; the orchestrator files them. Upstream implementation bugs (OpenMLS, tls_codec, mls-rs) are separate: label upstream. Never file anything externally without Mark's per-action OK.
